source.stem:
Multiple choice questions.

System of equations

$$
\left\{ \begin{array}{l} 3 x + 4 y = 5, \\ - 7 x + 9 y = - \frac {5}{2} \end{array} \right.
$$

The solution is ( ).

(A) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = 2,\\ y = -0.25 \end{array} \right.$

(B) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = -5.5,\\ y = 4 \end{array} \right.$

(C) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = 1,\\ y = 0.5 \end{array} \right.$

(D) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = -1,\\ y = -0.5 \end{array} \right.$

mx.name: term_substitution
mx.teacher_note: Uncrossed number is the label that belongs on this item, so 'Use the Sieve of Eratosthenes to separate primes from composites' is answered as uncrossed number rather than Sieve of Eratosthenes.

mx.name: relationship_reversal
mx.teacher_note: Remaining circled primes is what produces successive crossing out of multiples, so the usual direction of this relation is run backwards — on the item about Use the Sieve of Eratosthenes to separate primes from.

mx.name: mechanism_conflation
mx.teacher_note: Sieve of Eratosthenes is settled by running 'Decide whether one factor pair is enough to prove that two numbers': One chosen factorisation of each number can miss a common factor; to prove two numbers — on the item about Use the Sieve of Eratosthenes to separate primes from.

mx.name: operation_confusion
mx.teacher_note: Sieve of Eratosthenes is found by dividing the given values instead of multiplying, giving 17 as the reported result — on the item about Use the Sieve of Eratosthenes to separate primes from.

intelligence.enrichment: In the sieve, 1 is crossed out, each next uncrossed number is circled as prime, and its later multiples are crossed out; circled numbers are primes and crossed-out numbers other than 1 are composites.
